slides.heading: Line Through Points
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Arrays
slides.narration: Let's solve Line Through Points, a very hard arrays problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Maximum number of the given (unique, integer) points lying on one straight line.
For each anchor, count normalised slopes (reduced by gcd, sign-canonicalised).
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Maximum number of the given (unique, integer) points lying on one straight line. For each anchor, count normalised slopes (reduced by gcd, sign-canonicalised).

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Fix an anchor point; points on the same line through it share a normalised slope.
slides.narration: Fix an anchor point; points on the same line through it share a normalised slope.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Every pair defines a line, count points on it → O(n³)
Reduce slopes by gcd to avoid floats
slides.narration: Checking each pair's line against every point is cubic. Anchoring at each point and grouping the others by slope is quadratic.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. For each anchor, map slopes to counts
2. Normalise slopes with gcd and sign
3. Track the largest count plus one
slides.narration: Step by step. First, for each anchor, map slopes to counts. Second, normalise slopes with gcd and sign. Third, track the largest count plus one.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Anchor (1, 1)
slides.narration: Anchor at (1, 1): group the other points by reduced slope. The biggest group plus the anchor gives 3 points on one line. Best so far 3.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Anchor (2, 2)
slides.narration: Anchor at (2, 2): group the other points by reduced slope. The biggest group plus the anchor gives 4 points on one line. Best so far 4.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Anchor (3, 3)
slides.narration: Anchor at (3, 3): group the other points by reduced slope. The biggest group plus the anchor gives 2 points on one line. Best so far 4.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: For each anchor, we compute reduced dx and dy to every later point, normalise the sign, count in a map, and track the best count plus one.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n squared. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Floating-point slopes are risky; use reduced integer pairs with normalised signs.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: If duplicates are allowed, count them separately.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Fix an anchor point; points on the same line through it share a normalised slope.
